audience_question: What does the pilot evidence support the steering group doing next?
form: single annotated slide: summary range bar, 18-plot count grid, and a supported vs. not-supported split
fit_rationale: The brief gives only summary figures (median +6%, range -3% to +14%, 12 of 18 positive), not per-plot values, so a plot-level dot plot would invent data. A range bar with a zero reference line and an 18-cell count grid show the spread and the count without fabricating points. A two-column split separates what the group can decide now (another measurement cycle) from what the evidence does not support (wider installation on yield alone, a causal claim), which answers the question directly on one slide.
tradeoff: Per-plot magnitudes are not shown: the count grid shows how many plots were positive, not how large each difference was, so the reader sees the spread only as a summary range and median.
caveats: Pilot size: 18 greenhouse plots at three sites over one winter growing cycle.
Median yield difference vs. each site's reference plots was +6%; individual plot differences ranged from -3% to +14%.
12 of 18 plots had a positive yield difference; 6 did not.
Plots were not randomly assigned; crop mix and baseline conditions differed between sites.
The pilot does not show that lighting caused the observed yield differences.
Installation cost and energy use were not measured; yield alone does not support wider installation.
The steering group has not approved wider installation; it can authorize another measurement cycle.
Fictional scenario; all figures are invented for the evaluation.
